headings.title: SMTO-GML-0045 — SMTO can't find the Gmail sign-in app you named

html:
SMTO-GML-0045 — SMTO can't find the Gmail sign-in app you named

GUID: d3fa884a-f51f-4375-9183-83bf4d7716cc
Slug: gmail-oauth-app-missing
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • To connect Gmail, SMTO needs a saved Gmail OAuth App entry (your Google sign-in app details). The name you used, or the one your saved Gmail account points to, doesn't exist. Nothing in Gmail was touched.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select More options › Parameter Store and search for the app name you used. Check the spelling against your Gmail OAuth App entries. SMTO only accepts the exact saved name, so a small typo makes the app look missing.
  2. If no entry exists, create one with the Gmail OAuth App template and fill in the client ID and client secret from your Google Cloud project. If a saved Gmail account used an app that was deleted, reuse that same old name. A saved Gmail account remembers its app by name, so the new entry must carry that name for the account to keep working.
  3. In the conversation, ask SMTO to connect Gmail with that app, for example 'Connect Gmail using @gmail_auth_app and save the account as work_gmail', and finish the Google sign-in in your browser. Connecting again links your Gmail account to the app entry that now exists.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in page opens, and afterwards SMTO reports your Gmail account as connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the app name you used, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the client secret into the conversation, and don't keep repeating the request with the same name.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GmailParameterProfiles.resolve found no Parameter Store record for the requested gmail_oauth_app key (named in gmail.connect, or in a saved Gmail account's oauth_app_ref during token refresh).

What this means

  • GmailParameterProfiles.resolve looks up the exact gmail_oauth_app key and finds no stored record. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • GmailParameterProfiles.resolve looks up the exact gmail_oauth_app key and finds no stored record.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify the exact app key bound to the intended account before creating or selecting a replacement.

How to fix it

  • Check the key in Parameter Store (/parameter-editor): no record exists under that exact normalized key. Create it from the Gmail OAuth App template (client_type, client_id, client_secret, scopes) under the same key a saved gmail_account's oauth_app_ref names, or pass the correct existing key to gmail.connect, then reconnect the account.
  • Select or create the exact Gmail OAuth application parameter, then reconnect the intended account.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate current app profile exists and the intended account connects through it.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
